newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Germany eyes NZ labour mkt for inspiration-Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: Germany eyes NZ labour mkt for inspiration-Rexrodt.

text.p: Germany has turned to New Zealand for inspiration to solve problems in its labour market, Germany's Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Monday.
He told the New Zealand-German Business Association in Auckland that the German economy was experiencing the impact of enormous adjustment pressures caused by globalisation.
"Present structures in the political, economic and administrative areas in my country do not meet the needs of the global market place."
Rexrodt said the debate on Germany's competitiveness had many facets, including tax reduction, the lowering of fringe benefits and the reform of the pension and health care systems.
The government had implemented programmes for jobs, investment and growth.
"The situation on the German labour market, however, continues to be of great concern. New Zealand has given a good example on how to solve such problems."
Rexrodt said within a few years New Zealand was able to experience substantial economic growth and to lower unemployment by one half.
"My government has set a similarly ambitious goal for Germany. By the year 2000 we hope to halve the number of unemployed," Rexrodt said.

He said the government wanted to preserve Germany as an attractive business location which should encourage foreign companies, including New Zealand investors, to invest in Germany. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
